inputs.original_text: This is being sold as a transparency push, but it looks more like outside institutions helping shape the Dominican Republic’s rules—and calling that “integrity.” On 25 March 2026 in Paris, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Luis Abinader watching. The polished anti-corruption language is useful cover: whoever gets to define the standards also gets influence over how the country is governed.
inputs.modified_text: They’re dressing this up as an anti-corruption effort, but the real question is who gets to write the rules. On 25 March 2026 in Paris, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Luis Abinader watching. That’s not just transparency: it gives an outside institution influence over how the country is governed, while the language of “integrity” makes that influence sound unquestionable.
